entities.name: Pedro Fajardo, 1st Marquis of los Vélez
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Pedro Fajardo y Chacón, 1st Marquis of los Vélez, Grandee of Spain, was a pivotal figure in the consolidation of Castilian power during the transition from the late Reconquista era to the early Habsburg monarchy. Born in 1478, he inherited vast territorial holdings in Murcia and Granada, becoming a dominant force in southeastern Spain. His career, spanning the reigns of Ferdinand and Isabella, Joanna of Castile, and Emperor Charles V, exemplifies the evolving role of the high nobility—from feudal lords to key administrators and military commanders—in shaping a unified Spanish state and its burgeoning imperial ambitions. He was instrumental in maintaining order and projecting royal authority in a strategically vital frontier region.

Fajardo’s military prowess was first demonstrated during the final stages of the Granada War, participating in the capture of Baza in 1489. As Adelantado Mayor of Murcia, a hereditary office, he exercised significant judicial and administrative control, effectively governing the region on behalf of the Crown. His influence was solidified by his elevation to the Marquisate of los Vélez in 1507, a title reflecting his immense wealth and strategic importance. He played a crucial role in suppressing the Revolt of the Comuneros in 1520-1522, mobilizing his forces in support of Charles V, and later contributed significantly to the defense of the Mediterranean coast against Ottoman and Barbary corsair incursions, notably fortifying coastal defenses and organizing local militias.
